message.content:
In our own Solar System, **Jupiter** is the biggest planet—about 1 000 times more massive than Earth and roughly 11 times its diameter.

When you look beyond the Solar System, astronomers have found some truly gigantic worlds. The current record‑holder is an exoplanet called **HD 100546 b**, which is estimated to be about **20–25 times the mass of Jupiter** (roughly 0.02–0.025 solar masses). That makes it one of the most massive “planet‑like” objects ever discovered, though it sits right on the boundary between giant planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs.

So:

| Context | Largest Known |
|---------|---------------|
| Solar System | Jupiter |
| Exoplanets (planet‑class) | HD 100546 b (~20–25 M_Jup) |

(If you’re interested in even bigger objects, the next step up are brown dwarfs and stars, which can be tens to hundreds of times more massive.)
